title: A Ninja Breaks a 12-Year-Old's Arm and Still Can't Make Him Surrender

cuts.voiceover_text: At the final phase of the Hunter Exam, the rules are simple: you win only when your opponent surrenders, and killing your opponent means instant disqualification. The first match is announced. Hanzo, a bald ninja, versus Gon, a twelve-year-old boy in green. The two fighters step onto the arena floor as the other applicants watch from the sidelines.

The referee gives the signal, and Gon charges straight at Hanzo in a blur. The ninja slips behind him effortlessly and drops him with a single chop to the back of the neck, and Gon crashes face-first to the floor as his friends watch in shock. The boy pushes himself up, insisting he could have dodged that blow, but Hanzo hauls him up by the jacket and tells him that in a regular match, he would already have been declared the winner.

The one-sided beating stretches on for three whole hours, and still Gon will not say the words. So Hanzo escalates. He grabs Gon's left arm and breaks it, and the boy's scream echoes through the exam hall while his friends can only watch, forbidden from interfering. Even writhing on the floor with a broken arm, Gon refuses to surrender.

The stalemate drags on until Hanzo presses the blade hidden in his forearm to Gon's forehead and asks if the boy's pride is truly worth dying for. Gon answers that his father is a Hunter, that he took this exam so he could meet him someday, and that if he surrenders here, he feels he will never find him. Hanzo gives the ultimatum one last time: surrender or die. Gon does not even blink as blood drips from the cut on his brow. And it is Hanzo who breaks first. Shaken, the ninja pulls the blade away and gives up the match, saying he will take his chances in the next round.
When Gon protests that he does not want to win this way, Hanzo answers with a single strike that knocks the boy out cold, then tells the referee to move on to the next match.
With Hanzo's concession, Gon's victory is assured. Referees rush to the boy lying unconscious on the arena floor while Killua watches with furious concern, and the tournament moves on without him.
